nodes.label: Frame Compression (minor 6.3)
nodes.rationale: Negotiated then opportunistic: a frame is compressed only when the partner advertises >= 6.3, the payload is >= 1 KiB, and the compressed form is actually smaller, so tiny or incompressible bodies are never enlarged. zstd level 3 is the throughput/ratio sweet spot. Enriched directory views are the target, compressing roughly 7x on a realistic media library, which directly speeds cold WAN crawls. Compression happens after Postcard encoding and after chunk packing so the frame limit and paging are measured uncompressed; decompression output is bounded to MAX_FRAME_SIZE as a decompression-bomb guard.

nodes.label: Streamed Directory-View Pagination (minor 6.1)
nodes.rationale: A projection larger than one 1 MiB frame streams as DirectoryViewStart / Chunk(s) / End from one revision-consistent server snapshot, so there is no cursor to expire and no cross-page skew; the client reassembles an identical DirectoryView so callers above the transport see one result either way. An entry too large for one chunk sheds its inline xattr values (still reachable via GetXattr). Both peers cap the materialized set at MAX_DIRECTORY_ENTRIES (1,048,576) as a memory backstop.

nodes.label: Metadata Batching (minor 6.4)
nodes.rationale: A cold crawl otherwise pays a full RTT per GetMetadata, which dominates WAN latency even with readdirplus-style enrichment. GetMetadataBatch resolves up to 4096 nodes per round trip with positional results in request order; a per-node failure is reported in place as BatchedMetadata::Failed so one unresolved node never discards the rest. The 4096 cap keeps the reply inside one 1 MiB frame (no streaming path) and bounds server fan-out; an over-limit batch is rejected whole with TooLarge rather than truncated. The client emits it only when the server advertises >= 6.4 and otherwise falls back to per-node GetMetadata; the server needs no version check because it only receives.

nodes.label: Server Node Registry
nodes.rationale: Maps each opaque node UUID to its backing device+inode and known paths. Global entries whose refcount reaches zero are retained as a least-recently-found cache so reconnect keeps stable node IDs, and evicted lazily only under pressure. Each tracked node costs roughly 400-500 bytes.

nodes.label: Per-Connection and Global Known-Node Limits
nodes.rationale: Semaphore counters bounding the live working set, not the export size; their purpose is memory/DoS protection against a client that looks up nodes without ever forgetting them. Defaults were raised to 131072/524288 because macOS keeps a 100k-300k vnode cache and auto_xattr AppleDouble sidecars roughly double the working set during a crawl, so the old 8192/65536 were undersized.

nodes.label: Self-Healing Node Eviction
nodes.rationale: Neither ceiling is a hard wall. A full global pool evicts a globally-unreferenced cached entry and retries; an exhausted per-connection working set evicts one of its own nodes (skipping the root and any node backing an open handle) and retries. macOS reclaims vnodes lazily, so without this a long-lived mount would eventually fail every getattr/lookup of a new node with 'too many known nodes' (ErrorCode::TooLarge, surfaced as EFBIG) until remounted. Evicting only drops that connection's reference; the node stays in the larger global registry with an unchanged stable identifier, so nothing cached goes stale.

nodes.label: Aligned Read-Through Fill Sizing
nodes.rationale: Sequential/copy-sized reads align to the configured block up to the 16 MiB range limit, while sub-1 MiB probes use at most a 1 MiB aligned fill so Finder metadata/thumbnail inspection does not pull 16 MiB from every touched file. Server-side copy carries no raw body so the server can use reflink/copy-range acceleration without round-tripping bytes.
